## Counter

The old Counter is one number: `+` and `-` change it, `q` quits. The runner Counter has the same keys and two buttons. The facade Counter has buttons only (no key handler, no quit). The runner and facade folders also have two independent counters on one screen. The features are not the same in all variants, so compare the line counts with care.

### Counter: Current core (PRs 3-5, being replaced), Kyo

The whole app. `TuiApp` gives `main`.

```scala
// source: examples/src/main/scala/examples/counter/CounterApp.scala @ origin/feat/core-3-terminal, lines 1-25
package examples.counter

import tui4s.*

/** A number that `+` and `-` change; `q` quits (SPEC 3.1).
  *
  * Run it: `sbt "examples/runMain examples.counter.CounterApp"`.
  */
object CounterApp extends TuiApp[Int]:
    val keys: Keymap[Int] = Keymap(
      bind('+', "increment")(_ + 1),
      bind('-', "decrement")(_ - 1),
      bind('q', "quit")(_ => Quit),
    )

    def init: Int = 0

    def update(n: Int, event: Event): Next[Int] = keys(n, event)

    def view(n: Int): View =
      column(
        text("Count: ", n.toString.bold.yellow).centered.size(1),
        help(keys).centered.size(1),
      ).flex(Flex.Center).bordered(" Counter ")
end CounterApp
```

### Counter: kyo-ui + tui4s runner, hooks

Two blocks. Block 1 is the Counter in plain kyo-ui: it uses `Signal.initRef`, which is what `useSignal` calls (.work/proto/kyoui-runner/src/tui4s/kyoui/Hooks.scala:94-95). Block 2 is the same style with the tui4s name `useSignal`, and `component(...)`, which runs the hook at mount. The hooks code calls only these tui4s names: `Tui.run`, `Tui.quit`, `useSignal`, `component`. Block 3 is the main objects of block 2.

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-runner/apps/Counter.scala, lines 1-58
package apps

import kyo.*
import kyo.UI.*
import tui4s.kyoui.Tui

/** The Counter in plain kyo-ui: only kyo-ui's API, plus `Tui.quit` for the quit key. */
object Counter:

    val app: UI < Sync =
        for count <- Signal.initRef(0)
        yield div.onKeyDown {
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('+'), _, _) => count.updateAndGet(_ + 1)
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('-'), _, _) => count.updateAndGet(_ - 1)
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('q'), _, _) => Tui.quit
            case _                                       => ()
        }(
            h1("Counter"),
            span("Count: ", count.map(_.toString)).id("count"),
            div.style(_.row.gap(1.px))(
                button("+").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ + 1)),
                button("-").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ - 1))
            ),
            p("+ / - change it, Tab moves, Enter presses, q quits").style(_.color(Style.Color.gray))
        )

    /** One counter as a function: its state is allocated when the function runs. */
    def counter(label: String): UI < Sync =
        for count <- Signal.initRef(0)
        yield div.style(_.border(1.px, Style.Color.slate).padding(0.px, 1.px))(
            span(label).style(_.bold),
            span("Count: ", count.map(_.toString)),
            div.style(_.row.gap(1.px))(
                button("+").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ + 1)),
                button("-").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ - 1))
            )
        )

    /** Two independent counters side by side. */
    val twoCounters: UI < Sync =
        for
            left  <- counter("Left")
            right <- counter("Right")
        yield div.onKeyDown {
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('q'), _, _) => Tui.quit
            case _                                       => ()
        }(
            h1("Two counters"),
            div.style(_.row.gap(2.px))(left, right),
            p("Tab moves between the four buttons, Enter presses, q quits").style(_.color(Style.Color.gray))
        )
end Counter

object CounterMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(Counter.app))

object TwoCountersMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(Counter.twoCounters))
```

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-runner/apps/CounterStyles.scala, lines 1-46
package apps

import kyo.*
import kyo.UI.*
import tui4s.kyoui.Component
import tui4s.kyoui.Hooks.*
import tui4s.kyoui.Tui

/** Style 1: hooks. A component is a function that returns `UI < Sync` (or `< (Async & Scope)`). */
object CounterHooks:

    def counter(label: String): UI < Sync =
        for count <- useSignal(0)
        yield div.style(_.border(1.px, Style.Color.slate).padding(0.px, 1.px))(
            span(label).style(_.bold),
            span("Count: ", count.map(_.toString)),
            div.style(_.row.gap(1.px))(
                button("+").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ + 1)),
                button("-").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ - 1))
            )
        )

    /** Sequenced at the top: each call allocates its own state once. */
    val app: UI < Sync =
        for
            left  <- counter("Left")
            right <- counter("Right")
        yield div.onKeyDown {
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('q'), _, _) => Tui.quit
            case _                                       => ()
        }(h1("Hooks"), div.style(_.row.gap(2.px))(left, right))

    /** The same, mounted by the runner: `component(...)` runs the effect when the node mounts. Here the counters live
      * inside a `when`: hiding them drops their state, showing them again starts from 0.
      */
    val dynamic: UI < Sync =
        for shown <- useSignal(true)
        yield div.onKeyDown {
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('h'), _, _) => shown.updateAndGet(!_)
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('q'), _, _) => Tui.quit
            case _                                       => ()
        }(
            h1("Hooks, mounted by the runner (h hides/shows)"),
            when(shown)(div.style(_.row.gap(2.px))(component(counter("Left")), component(counter("Right"))))
        )
end CounterHooks
```

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-runner/apps/CounterStyles.scala, lines 71-75
object CounterHooksMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(CounterHooks.app))

object CounterHooksDynamicMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(CounterHooks.dynamic))
```

```scala
/** Style 2: a component class with a type member for its state. The runner allocates the state at mount. */
final class CounterBox(label: String) extends Component:
    type State = Int
    def initial: Int = 0
    def view(count: SignalRef[Int]): UI =
        div.style(_.border(1.px, Style.Color.slate).padding(0.px, 1.px))(
            span(label).style(_.bold),
            span("Count: ", count.map(_.toString)),
            div.style(_.row.gap(1.px))(
                button("+").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ + 1)),
                button("-").onClick(count.updateAndGet(_ - 1))
            )
        )
end CounterBox

object CounterComponents:
    val app: UI =
        div.onKeyDown {
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('q'), _, _) => Tui.quit
            case _                                       => ()
        }(h1("Components"), div.style(_.row.gap(2.px))(CounterBox("Left"), CounterBox("Right")))
end CounterComponents
```

### Counter: ZIO facade (generated mirror)

Hooks style (`Counter`) and class style (`CounterComponent`) in one file (block 1). The facades prototype has no terminal entry point. The integration prototype adds one (block 2). Blocks 3 and 4 show how the facade test starts the app on the headless test runner.

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-facades/zio/apps/Counter.scala, lines 1-41
package apps.zio

import tui4s.interop.zio.ui.*
import zio.*

/** Counter, hooks style. No Kyo type, no Kyo import. */
object Counter:
    def apply(label: String, key: String): ZIO[Scope, Nothing, HtmlNode] =
        for count <- useSignal(0)
        yield div(
            h1(label),
            count.render(n => p(s"Count: $n")),
            button("-").id(s"$key-dec").onClick(count.update(_ - 1)),
            button("+").id(s"$key-inc").onClick(count.update(_ + 1))
        )
end Counter

/** Counter, Component class style: the runner allocates `State` at mount. */
object CounterComponent extends Component:
    type State = Int
    def initial = 0

    // claude 2026-10-03: changed the state type to the facade's SignalRef
    def view(count: SignalRef[Int]): HtmlNode =
        div(
            h1("Component counter"),
            count.render(n => p(s"Count: $n")),
            button("+").id("c-inc").onClick(count.update(_ + 1)),
            button("reset").id("c-reset").onClick(count.set(0))
        )
end CounterComponent

/** Two independent counters and a component counter on one screen. */
object CounterApp:
    val app: ZIO[Scope, Nothing, UI] =
        for
            a <- Counter("Left", "a")
            b <- Counter("Right", "b")
            c <- CounterComponent.mount
        yield div(a, b, c)
end CounterApp
```

### Counter: Cats facade (generated mirror)

Tagless final: `F[_]: Async`. Hooks style and class style in one file (block 1). The integration prototype adds the terminal entry point (block 2). Blocks 3 and 4 show how the facade test starts the app.

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-facades/cats/apps/Counter.scala, lines 1-41
package apps.cats

import cats.effect.*
import fs2.concurrent.SignallingRef
import tui4s.interop.cats.ui.*

/** Counter, hooks style, for any F with an Async. No Kyo type, no Kyo import. */
object Counter:
    def apply[F[_]: Async](label: String, key: String): Resource[F, HtmlNode] =
        for count <- useSignal[F](0)
        yield div(
            h1(label),
            count.render(n => p(s"Count: $n")),
            button("-").id(s"$key-dec").onClick(count.update(_ - 1)),
            button("+").id(s"$key-inc").onClick(count.update(_ + 1))
        )
end Counter

/** Counter, Component class style: the runner allocates `State` at mount. */
final class CounterComponent[F[_]: Async] extends Component[F]:
    type State = Int
    def initial = 0

    def view(count: SignallingRef[F, Int]): HtmlNode =
        div(
            h1("Component counter"),
            count.render(n => p(s"Count: $n")),
            button("+").id("c-inc").onClick(count.update(_ + 1)),
            button("reset").id("c-reset").onClick(count.set(0))
        )
end CounterComponent

/** Two independent counters and a component counter on one screen, in IO. */
object CounterApp:
    val app: Resource[IO, UI] =
        for
            a <- Counter[IO]("Left", "a")
            b <- Counter[IO]("Right", "b")
            c <- CounterComponent[IO]().mount
        yield div(a, b, c)
end CounterApp
```

The mirror's `onClick(action: ZIO[Any, Nothing, Any])` (zio/generated/ZioUi.scala:246-247) wraps the ZIO with `Bridge.action`, which runs it on the runtime of the fiber that mounted the UI. ## Todo

The old Todo and the runner Todo both have a text input, a list with a cursor, toggle, delete, file load and Ctrl-S save. The facade Todo has no file, no cursor and no quit key: it has an Add button, a checkbox and a delete button per row, and a "Clear done" button. So the facade line counts are for less work.

### Todo: Current core (PRs 3-5, being replaced), Kyo

The whole app: the state, a file store in plain Kyo, the keymaps per pane, the view.

```scala
// source: examples/src/main/scala/examples/todo/TodoApp.scala @ origin/feat/core-3-terminal, lines 1-176
package examples.todo

import java.io.IOException
import java.nio.file.Files
import java.nio.file.Path
import kyo.*
import scala.jdk.CollectionConverters.*
import tui4s.*

enum Pane derives CanEqual:
    case Input, Items

final case class Item(title: String, done: Boolean = false) derives CanEqual

final case class Todo(
    field: TextField = TextField.empty,
    items: Vector[Item] = Vector.empty,
    selected: Int = 0,
    focus: Focus[Pane] = Focus(Pane.Input, Pane.Items),
    ready: Boolean = false,
    status: String = "loading…",
) derives CanEqual:
    def left: Int = items.count(!_.done)

    def add: Todo =
      if field.isBlank then this
      else
          copy(
            field = TextField.empty,
            items = items :+ Item(field.text.trim),
            selected = items.size,
          )

    def move(by: Int): Todo =
      copy(selected = (selected + by).max(0).min((items.size - 1).max(0)))

    def toggle: Todo =
      if items.isEmpty then this
      else
          copy(items =
            items.updated(
              selected,
              items(selected).copy(done = !items(selected).done),
            ),
          )

    def delete: Todo =
      if items.isEmpty then this
      else
          val rest = items.patch(selected, Nil, 1)
          copy(items = rest, selected = selected.min((rest.size - 1).max(0)))

    def nextPane: Todo = copy(focus = focus.next)

    def typed(event: Event): Todo =
        val f = field.edit(event)
        // The same object when the key did nothing: no frame.
        if f eq field then this else copy(field = f)

    def loaded(r: Result[IOException, Vector[Item]]): Todo = r match
        case Result.Success(items) =>
          copy(items = items, ready = true, status = s"${items.size} loaded")
        case failed                =>
          copy(ready = true, status = s"could not load: $failed")

    def saved(r: Result[IOException, Unit]): Todo = r match
        case Result.Success(_) => copy(status = "saved")
        case failed            => copy(status = s"could not save: $failed")
end Todo

/** Plain Kyo code. It knows nothing about tui4s. */
object TodoStore:
    val file: Path =
      Path.of(java.lang.System.getProperty("user.home"), ".tui4s-todo.txt")

    def load(using Frame): Vector[Item] < (Sync & Abort[IOException]) =
      Abort.catching[IOException](Sync.defer {
        if !Files.exists(file) then Vector.empty
        else
            Files
              .readAllLines(file)
              .asScala
              .toVector
              .map(l => Item(l.drop(4), done = l.startsWith("[x]")))
      })

    def save(
        items: Vector[Item],
    )(using Frame): Unit < (Sync & Abort[IOException]) =
      Abort
        .catching[IOException](Sync.defer {
          Files.write(
            file,
            items.map(i => (if i.done then "[x] " else "[ ] ") + i.title).asJava,
          )
        })
        .unit
end TodoStore

/** A text input, a list with a selection, `space` toggles, `d` deletes, `tab`
  * moves the focus; the list loads at start and Ctrl-S saves it (SPEC 3.2).
  *
  * Run it: `sbt "examples/runMain examples.todo.TodoApp"`.
  */
object TodoApp extends TuiApp[Todo]:
    val global: Keymap[Todo] = Keymap(
      bind(Key.Tab, "focus")(_.nextPane).or(Key.BackTab),
      bind(Key.Ctrl('s'), "save")(save),
      bind(Key.Esc, "quit")(_ => Quit),
    )

    // The pane keys first, so the help bar lists them first.
    val inputKeys: Keymap[Todo] =
      Keymap(bind(Key.Enter, "add")(_.add)) ++ global

    val itemKeys: Keymap[Todo] = Keymap(
      bind(Key.Up, "up")(_.move(-1)).or('k'),
      bind(Key.Down, "down")(_.move(1)).or('j'),
      bind(' ', "toggle")(_.toggle),
      bind('d', "delete")(_.delete),
      bind('q', "quit")(_ => Quit),
    ) ++ global

    def keys(t: Todo): Keymap[Todo] =
      if t.focus.is(Pane.Input) then inputKeys else itemKeys

    def init: Todo = Todo()

    /** Load once at start: the initial state declares the task; its fold sets
      * `ready`, which removes it.
      */
    override def sources(t: Todo): Seq[Source[Todo]] =
      if t.ready then Nil
      else
          Seq(
            source
              .task(Abort.run[IOException](TodoStore.load))(_.loaded(_))
              .id("load"),
          )

    /** One-shot: the state says "saving…", the task writes the file and folds
      * the result. With an id, a second Ctrl-S replaces a save that is still
      * running (latest wins).
      */
    private def save(t: Todo): Next[Todo] =
      t.copy(status = "saving…")
        .withTask(
          source
            .task(Abort.run[IOException](TodoStore.save(t.items)))(_.saved(_))
            .id("save"),
        )

    def update(t: Todo, event: Event): Next[Todo] =
        val active = keys(t)
        event match
            case active(action)              => action(t)
            // The rest is text: 'q' and 'd' type letters here.
            case e if t.focus.is(Pane.Input) => t.typed(e)
            case _                           => t

    def view(t: Todo): View =
        val inInput = t.focus.is(Pane.Input)
        column(
          input(t.field, focused = inInput, placeholder = "What needs doing?")
            .bordered(" New ", focused = inInput)
            .size(3),
          list(t.items.map(itemLine), t.selected, focused = !inInput)
            .bordered(s" Todo · ${t.left} left ", focused = !inInput),
          row(help(keys(t)), text(t.status.dim).right.size(24)).size(1),
        )
    end view

    private def itemLine(item: Item): Line =
      if item.done then line("✔ ".green, item.title.dim.crossedOut)
      else line("☐ ", item.title)
end TodoApp
```

### Todo: kyo-ui + tui4s runner, hooks

Plain kyo-ui. The state is made with `Signal.initRef` in one `for` (the hooks style). Components are plain functions of signals and actions.

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-runner/apps/Todo.scala, lines 1-114
package apps

import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
import java.nio.file.Files
import java.nio.file.Paths
import kyo.*
import kyo.UI.*
import tui4s.kyoui.Tui

/** The Todo app in plain kyo-ui. Components are plain functions of signals and actions. */
object Todo:

    final case class Item(id: Int, text: String, done: Boolean) derives CanEqual
    final case class Row(item: Item, selected: Boolean) derives CanEqual

    // ---- file ----

    def parse(lines: Chunk[String]): Chunk[Item] =
        lines.filter(_.length >= 4).zipWithIndex.map((l, i) => Item(i + 1, l.drop(4), l.startsWith("[x]")))

    def render(items: Chunk[Item]): String =
        items.map(t => s"${if t.done then "[x]" else "[ ]"} ${t.text}").mkString("", "\n", "\n")

    def load(file: String)(using Frame): Chunk[Item] < Sync =
        Abort.run[java.io.IOException](Abort.catching[java.io.IOException] {
            val p = Paths.get(file)
            if Files.exists(p) then Chunk.from(Files.readAllLines(p, StandardCharsets.UTF_8).toArray.map(_.toString)) else Chunk.empty
        }).map(r => parse(r.getOrElse(Chunk.empty)))

    def save(file: String, items: Chunk[Item])(using Frame): Unit < (Sync & Abort[java.io.IOException]) =
        Abort.catching[java.io.IOException](Files.writeString(Paths.get(file), render(items), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)).unit

    // ---- components ----

    def header(count: Signal[String]): UI =
        div.style(_.row.gap(2.px))(h1("Todo"), span(count).style(_.color(Style.Color.gray)))

    def inputBar(draft: SignalRef[String], add: => Any < Async): UI =
        form.onSubmit(add)(
            div.style(_.row.gap(1.px))(
                span("New:"),
                input.id("draft").placeholder("What needs doing? (Enter adds)").value(draft).style(_.width(40.px))
            )
        )

    def row(r: Row): Ast.Li =
        li.style(if r.selected then Style.bg(Style.Color.indigo).color(Style.Color.white) else Style.empty)(
            checkbox.checked(r.item.done),
            span(" " + r.item.text).style(if r.item.done then Style.strikethrough.color(Style.Color.gray) else Style.empty)
        )

    def list(rows: Signal[Chunk[Row]], onKey: KeyboardEvent => Any < Async): UI =
        ul.id("list").tabIndex(0).onKeyDown(onKey)
            .style(_.border(1.px, Style.Color.slate).minHeight(4.px).focus(_.border(1.px, Style.Color.blue)))(
                rows.foreachKeyed(_.item.id.toString)(row)
            )

    def footer(status: Signal[String]): UI =
        div(
            span(status).id("status").style(_.color(Style.Color.green)),
            span("Tab: input/list  ↑↓: move  Space: toggle  d: delete  Ctrl-S: save  Esc: quit").style(_.color(Style.Color.gray))
        )

    // ---- the app ----

    def app(file: String): UI < (Async & Scope) =
        for
            loaded <- load(file)
            items  <- Signal.initRef(loaded)
            draft  <- Signal.initRef("")
            cursor <- Signal.initRef(0)
            status <- Signal.initRef(s"loaded ${loaded.size} items from $file")
            nextId <- AtomicInt.init(loaded.size + 1)
            rows  = items.combineLatest(cursor).map((ts, c) => ts.zipWithIndex.map((t, i) => Row(t, i == c)))
            count = items.map(ts => s"${ts.count(!_.done)} open / ${ts.size}")
            add = draft.get.map { text =>
                if text.trim.isEmpty then ()
                else nextId.getAndIncrement.map(id => items.updateAndGet(_ :+ Item(id, text.trim, false))).andThen(draft.set(""))
            }
            atCursor = (f: (Chunk[Item], Int) => Chunk[Item]) =>
                cursor.get.map(c => items.updateAndGet(ts => if c >= 0 && c < ts.size then f(ts, c) else ts))
            toggle = atCursor((ts, c) => ts.updated(c, ts(c).copy(done = !ts(c).done)))
            delete = atCursor((ts, c) => ts.take(c) ++ ts.drop(c + 1)).map(ts => cursor.updateAndGet(c => c.min(ts.size - 1).max(0)))
            move   = (d: Int) => items.get.map(ts => cursor.updateAndGet(c => (c + d).max(0).min((ts.size - 1).max(0))))
            // The result type is load-bearing: without it the match widens to `Any` and kyo lifts the effects as plain
            // values, so they never run (the "lift trap"; see REPORT.md section 5).
            listKeys = (e: KeyboardEvent) =>
                (e.key match
                    case Keyboard.ArrowUp | Keyboard.Char('k')   => move(-1)
                    case Keyboard.ArrowDown | Keyboard.Char('j') => move(1)
                    case Keyboard.Space                          => toggle
                    case Keyboard.Char('d')                      => delete
                    case _                                       => ()
                ): Any < Async
            saveAll = items.get.map(ts =>
                Abort.run[java.io.IOException](save(file, ts)).map {
                    case Result.Success(_) => status.set(s"saved ${ts.size} items to $file")
                    case other             => status.set(s"save failed: $other")
                }
            )
        yield main.onKeyDown {
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('s'), mods, _) if mods.ctrl => saveAll
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Escape, _, _)                    => Tui.quit
            case _                                                       => ()
        }(
            header(count),
            inputBar(draft, add),
            list(rows, listKeys),
            footer(status)
        )
end Todo

object TodoMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(Todo.app(sys.env.getOrElse("TODO_FILE", "todos.txt"))))
```

Hooks style (block 1). Block 2 is the terminal entry point of the integration prototype. Block 3 shows how the facade test starts the app.

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-facades/zio/apps/Todo.scala, lines 1-47
package apps.zio

import tui4s.interop.zio.ui.*
import zio.*

final case class Todo(id: Int, title: String, done: Boolean)

/** Todo, hooks style: a two-way bound input, Enter or a button to add, a keyed list with checkboxes. */
object TodoApp:
    val app: ZIO[Scope, Nothing, HtmlNode] =
        for
            todos  <- useSignal(List.empty[Todo])
            draft  <- useSignal("")
            nextId <- Ref.make(1)
        yield
            val add: UIO[Unit] =
                for
                    title <- draft.get
                    _ <- ZIO.when(title.trim.nonEmpty) {
                        nextId.getAndUpdate(_ + 1).flatMap(id => todos.update(_ :+ Todo(id, title.trim, false))) *>
                            draft.set("")
                    }
                yield ()

            def toggle(id: Int, done: Boolean): UIO[Unit] =
                todos.update(_.map(t => if t.id == id then t.copy(done = done) else t))

            div(
                h1("Todos"),
                input.id("new").placeholder("What needs doing?").value(draft)
                    .onKeyDown(e => ZIO.when(e.key == Keyboard.Enter)(add)),
                button("Add").id("add").onClick(add),
                ul(
                    todos.signal.foreachKeyed(_.id.toString)(t =>
                        li(
                            checkbox.id(s"done-${t.id}").checked(t.done).onChange(d => toggle(t.id, d)),
                            span(if t.done then s"~${t.title}~" else t.title),
                            button("x").id(s"del-${t.id}").onClick(todos.update(_.filterNot(_.id == t.id)))
                        )
                    )
                ),
                todos.render(ts => p(s"${ts.count(!_.done)} left")),
                when(todos.signal.map(_.exists(_.done)))(
                    button("Clear done").id("clear").onClick(todos.update(_.filterNot(_.done)))
                )
            )
end TodoApp
```

```scala
package apps.cats

import cats.effect.*
import cats.syntax.all.*
import tui4s.interop.cats.ui.*

final case class Todo(id: Int, title: String, done: Boolean)

/** Todo, hooks style, tagless final: a two-way bound input, Enter or a button to add, a keyed list with checkboxes. */
object TodoApp:
    def apply[F[_]: Async]: Resource[F, HtmlNode] =
        for
            todos  <- useSignal[F](List.empty[Todo])
            draft  <- useSignal[F]("")
            nextId <- Resource.eval(Ref.of[F, Int](1))
        yield
            val add: F[Unit] =
                draft.get.flatMap { title =>
                    (nextId.getAndUpdate(_ + 1).flatMap(id => todos.update(_ :+ Todo(id, title.trim, false))) *>
                        draft.set("")).whenA(title.trim.nonEmpty)
                }

            def toggle(id: Int, done: Boolean): F[Unit] =
                todos.update(_.map(t => if t.id == id then t.copy(done = done) else t))

            div(
                h1("Todos"),
                input.id("new").placeholder("What needs doing?").value(draft)
                    .onKeyDown(e => add.whenA(e.key == Keyboard.Enter)),
                button("Add").id("add").onClick(add),
                ul(
                    todos.signal.foreachKeyed(_.id.toString)(t =>
                        li(
                            checkbox.id(s"done-${t.id}").checked(t.done).onChange(d => toggle(t.id, d)),
                            span(if t.done then s"~${t.title}~" else t.title),
                            button("x").id(s"del-${t.id}").onClick(todos.update(_.filterNot(_.id == t.id)))
                        )
                    )
                ),
                todos.render(ts => p(s"${ts.count(!_.done)} left")),
                when(todos.signal.map(_.exists(_.done)))(
                    button("Clear done").id("clear").onClick(todos.update(_.filterNot(_.done)))
                )
            )
end TodoApp
```

## Dashboard

The old Dashboard has 2 tabs (Metrics, Requests), a gauge and a sparkline fed by a poller every 250 ms, a log pane fed by a stream, `p` pauses the poller, `q` quits. The runner Dashboard has 3 tabs (CPU, Memory, Network), the same gauge, sparkline, log pane and keys. The old core draws the gauge, sparkline and tabs with jatatui widgets; the runner app draws them as text in `Widgets.scala` (plain kyo-ui), which is included and counted.

### Dashboard: Current core (PRs 3-5, being replaced), Kyo

The whole app. `sources(d)` is a function of the state.

```scala
// source: examples/src/main/scala/examples/dashboard/DashboardApp.scala @ origin/feat/core-3-terminal, lines 1-78
package examples.dashboard

import kyo.*
import tui4s.*

final case class Dash(
    tab: Int = 0,
    cpu: Double = 0.0,
    history: Vector[Long] = Vector.empty,
    logs: Vector[String] = Vector.empty,
    paused: Boolean = false,
) derives CanEqual:
    def sample(v: Double): Dash  =
      copy(cpu = v, history = (history :+ (v * 100).toLong).takeRight(200))
    def log(line: String): Dash  = copy(logs = (logs :+ line).takeRight(500))
    def switchTab(by: Int): Dash =
      copy(tab = Math.floorMod(tab + by, Dash.tabs.size))
    def togglePause: Dash        = copy(paused = !paused)
end Dash

object Dash:
    val tabs: Vector[String] = Vector("Metrics", "Requests")

/** Tabs, a gauge and a sparkline fed by a poller every 250 ms, and a log pane
  * fed by a stream (SPEC 3.3).
  *
  * Run it: `sbt "examples/runMain examples.dashboard.DashboardApp"`.
  */
object DashboardApp extends TuiApp[Dash]:
    /** Any Kyo stream. chunkSize = 1: with the default (4096) unfold buffers
      * lines before they emit.
      */
    val requests: Stream[String, Async] =
      Stream.unfold(1, chunkSize = 1)(i =>
        Async
          .sleep(700.millis)
          .andThen(Present((s"GET /api/items/$i 200", i + 1))),
      )

    val keys: Keymap[Dash] = Keymap(
      bind(Key.Left, "prev tab")(_.switchTab(-1)),
      bind(Key.Right, "next tab")(_.switchTab(1)),
      bind('p', "pause")(_.togglePause),
      bind('q', "quit")(_ => Quit),
    )

    def init: Dash = Dash()

    def update(d: Dash, event: Event): Next[Dash] = keys(d, event)

    /** A function of the state: pausing removes the poller, so its fiber stops;
      * the log stream keeps running.
      */
    override def sources(d: Dash): Seq[Source[Dash]] =
        val logs = source.stream(requests)(_.log(_)).id("logs")
        val cpu  =
          source.poll(250.millis)(Random.nextDouble)(_.sample(_)).id("cpu")
        if d.paused then Seq(logs) else Seq(logs, cpu)

    def view(d: Dash): View =
      column(
        tabs(Dash.tabs, d.tab).bordered(" Dashboard ").size(3),
        if d.tab == 0 then metrics(d)
        else logPane(d.logs).bordered(" Requests "),
        help(keys).size(1),
      )

    private def metrics(d: Dash): View =
      row(
        column(
          gauge(d.cpu, f"${d.cpu * 100}%.0f%%")
            .bordered(if d.paused then " CPU (paused) " else " CPU ")
            .size(3),
          sparkline(d.history, max = Some(100L)).bordered(" History "),
        ).percent(60),
        logPane(d.logs).bordered(" Requests "),
      )
end DashboardApp
```

```scala
) derives CanEqual:
    def sample(v: Double): Dash  =

    def log(line: String): Dash  = copy(logs = (logs :+ line).takeRight(500))
    def switchTab(by: Int): Dash =

end Dash

object Dash:
    val tabs: Vector[String] = Vector("Metrics", "Requests")

/** The Dashboard for ZIO users (SPEC 3.4): tabs, a gauge and a sparkline fed by
  * a ZIO poller every 250 ms, and a log pane fed by a `ZStream`. No Kyo type:
  * `ZStream`, `Schedule`, `Random` and `700.millis` are ZIO's.
  *
  * Run it: `sbt examples/launchers`, then `examples/target/bin/ziodashboard`.
  */
object DashboardApp extends TuiApp[Dash]:

      ZStream
        .iterate(1)(_ + 1)
        .schedule(Schedule.spaced(700.millis))
        .map(i => s"GET /api/items/$i 200")

    val keys: Keymap[Dash] = Keymap(
      bind(Key.Left, "prev tab")(_.switchTab(-1)),
      bind(Key.Right, "next tab")(_.switchTab(1)),
      bind('p', "pause")(_.togglePause),
      bind('q', "quit")(_ => Quit),
    )

    def init: Dash = Dash()

    def update(d: Dash, event: Event): Next[Dash] = keys(d, event)

    /** A function of the state: pausing removes the poller, so its ZIO is
      * interrupted; the log stream keeps running.
      */
    override def sources(d: Dash): Seq[Source[Dash]] =
        val logs = source.stream(requests)(_.log(_)).id("logs")
        val cpu  =
          source.poll(250.millis)(Random.nextDouble)(_.sample(_)).id("cpu")
        if d.paused then Seq(logs) else Seq(logs, cpu)

    def view(d: Dash): View =
      column(
        tabs(Dash.tabs, d.tab).bordered(" Dashboard ").size(3),
        if d.tab == 0 then metrics(d)
        else logPane(d.logs).bordered(" Requests "),
        help(keys).size(1),
      )

    private def metrics(d: Dash): View =
      row(
        column(
          gauge(d.cpu, f"${d.cpu * 100}%.0f%%")
            .bordered(if d.paused then " CPU (paused) " else " CPU ")
            .size(3),
          sparkline(d.history, max = Some(100L)).bordered(" History "),
        ).percent(60),
        logPane(d.logs).bordered(" Requests "),
      )
end DashboardApp
```

```scala
import cats.effect.IO

/** The Dashboard for Cats Effect users (SPEC 3.5): tabs, a gauge and a
  * sparkline fed by an `IO` that a poller runs every 250 ms, and a log pane fed

object DashboardApp extends TuiApp[Dash]:

        .iterate(1)(_ + 1)
        .covary[IO]

      * cancelled; the log stream keeps running.

    override def sources(d: Dash): Seq[Source[Dash]] =

        if d.paused then Seq(logs) else Seq(logs, cpu)
```

### Dashboard: kyo-ui + tui4s runner, hooks

Plain kyo-ui. Block 1 is the app. Block 2 is `Widgets.scala`: the gauge, sparkline and tabs, written as text spans in plain kyo-ui (they also render in a browser).

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-runner/apps/Dashboard.scala, lines 1-98
package apps

import kyo.*
import kyo.UI.*
import tui4s.kyoui.Tui

/** The Dashboard in plain kyo-ui: tabs (Left / Right), a gauge and a sparkline fed by a 250 ms sampler, a log pane fed by a
  * stream, `p` pauses the sampler (logs go on), `q` quits.
  */
object Dashboard:

    val series = Seq("CPU", "Memory", "Network")

    /** One sample of every series, and the last 40 samples of each. One ref, so one tick is one atomic change. */
    final case class Metrics(now: Chunk[Double], history: Chunk[Chunk[Double]]) derives CanEqual

    object Metrics:
        val empty: Metrics = Metrics(Chunk.fill(series.size)(0.0), Chunk.fill(series.size)(Chunk.empty))

    final case class State(
        tab: SignalRef[Int],
        metrics: SignalRef[Metrics],
        paused: SignalRef[Boolean],
        logs: SignalRef[Chunk[(Int, String)]]
    )

    def init(using Frame): State < Sync =
        for
            tab     <- Signal.initRef(0)
            metrics <- Signal.initRef(Metrics.empty)
            paused  <- Signal.initRef(false)
            logs    <- Signal.initRef(Chunk.empty[(Int, String)])
        yield State(tab, metrics, paused, logs)

    /** One sampler tick with given values (the bench calls this directly). */
    def tick(s: State, values: Chunk[Double])(using Frame): Unit < Sync =
        s.metrics.updateAndGet(m => Metrics(values, m.history.zip(values).map((h, v) => (h :+ v).takeRight(40)))).unit

    /** The sampler: a random walk every 250 ms, skipped while paused. */
    def sampler(s: State)(using Frame): Unit < Async =
        Loop.forever {
            Async.sleep(250.millis).andThen(s.paused.get).map { p =>
                if p then ()
                else
                    s.metrics.get.map { m =>
                        Kyo.foreach(m.now)(v => Random.nextDouble.map(r => (v + (r - 0.5) * 0.3).max(0).min(1))).map(vs => tick(s, vs))
                    }
            }
        }

    /** A log stream: one line every 400 ms. */
    def logStream(using Frame): Stream[String, Async] =
        Stream[String, Async] {
            Loop(1) { i =>
                Async.sleep(400.millis).andThen(Emit.valueWith(Chunk(s"event #$i: request served"))(Loop.continue(i + 1)))
            }
        }

    def overview(s: State): UI =
        s.tab.render { t =>
            div.style(_.border(1.px, Style.Color.slate).padding(0.px, 1.px))(
                h2(s"${series(t)} usage"),
                Widgets.gauge(s.metrics.map(_.now(t)), 30, Style.Color.green),
                Widgets.sparkline(s.metrics.map(_.history(t)), Style.Color.blue)
            )
        }

    def logPane(s: State): UI =
        div.style(_.border(1.px, Style.Color.slate).padding(0.px, 1.px).height(10.px))(
            h3("Log"),
            ul(s.logs.foreachKeyed(_._1.toString)((_, line) => li(line)))
        )

    def view(s: State): UI =
        div.onKeyDown {
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.ArrowLeft, _, _)  => s.tab.updateAndGet(t => (t + series.size - 1) % series.size)
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.ArrowRight, _, _) => s.tab.updateAndGet(t => (t + 1) % series.size)
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('p'), _, _)  => s.paused.updateAndGet(!_)
            case KeyboardEvent(Keyboard.Char('q'), _, _)  => Tui.quit
            case _                                        => ()
        }(
            div.style(_.row.gap(2.px))(h1("Dashboard"), Widgets.tabs(s.tab, series)),
            overview(s),
            logPane(s),
            span(s.paused.map(p => if p then "sampler PAUSED (p resumes)" else "sampler running (p pauses)  ←/→ tabs  q quits"))
                .style(_.color(Style.Color.gray))
        )

    val app: UI < (Async & Scope) =
        for
            s <- init
            _ <- Fiber.init(sampler(s))
            _ <- Fiber.init(logStream.foreach(line => s.logs.updateAndGet(l => (l :+ (l.lastOption.fold(1)(_._1 + 1), line)).takeRight(6))))
        yield view(s)
end Dashboard

object DashboardMain extends KyoApp:
    run(Tui.run(Dashboard.app))
```

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-runner/apps/Widgets.scala, lines 1-40
package apps

import kyo.*
import kyo.UI.*

/** Terminal-ish widgets written in PLAIN kyo-ui (spans of block characters), so they also render in a browser. */
object Widgets:

    private val blocks = "▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█"

    /** A horizontal gauge of `width` cells for a ratio in [0, 1]. */
    def gaugeText(ratio: Double, width: Int): String =
        val r      = ratio.max(0).min(1)
        val filled = (r * width).round.toInt
        "█" * filled + "░" * (width - filled) + f" ${r * 100}%3.0f%%"

    /** A sparkline: one block character per value, scaled to [lo, hi]. */
    def sparklineText(values: Chunk[Double], lo: Double = 0, hi: Double = 1): String =
        values.map { v =>
            val i = (((v - lo) / (hi - lo).max(1e-9)) * (blocks.length - 1)).round.toInt.max(0).min(blocks.length - 1)
            blocks.charAt(i)
        }.mkString

    def gauge(ratio: Signal[Double], width: Int, color: Style.Color): UI =
        ratio.render(r => span(gaugeText(r, width)).style(_.color(color)))

    def sparkline(values: Signal[Chunk[Double]], color: Style.Color): UI =
        values.render(vs => span(sparklineText(vs)).style(_.color(color)))

    /** Tabs: a row of buttons in one focus group (ArrowLeft / ArrowRight move between them); the selected one is bold. */
    def tabs(selected: SignalRef[Int], labels: Seq[String]): UI =
        selected.render { sel =>
            nav.style(_.gap(1.px))(
                fragment(labels.zipWithIndex.map { (l, i) =>
                    button(l).focusGroup("tabs").onClick(selected.set(i))
                        .style(if i == sel then Style.bold.color(Style.Color.yellow) else Style.color(Style.Color.gray))
                }*)
            )
        }
end Widgets
```

## Entry point on the terminal for the facade apps (integration prototype, DONE)

The folder `.work/proto/kyoui-integration/` holds the integration prototype. Its REPORT says DONE. It reuses the runner and facade sources with no change (`project.scala`: `//> using files`). It adds one `Tui` object per ecosystem (the glue), the mains and tests. A ZIO or Cats user starts a facade app with one call, `Tui.run(app)` (block 1). Blocks 2 and 3 are library glue, not app code: they show which types the user meets at the entry point.

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-integration/glue/zio/Tui.scala, lines 32-77 (library glue, not app code; integration prototype, DONE)
object Tui:

    /** The quit signal of the run that is active in this fiber (and in the fibers it forks: the handlers). */
    // claude 2026-10-03: created quitRef: a FiberRef, because a handler runs on a ZIO fiber that the facade forks from the
    // runtime captured by `AmbientZIOs.run`; that runtime carries this FiberRef, but not the Kyo Local of the runner.
    private val quitRef: FiberRef[Option[Promise[Nothing, Unit]]] =
        Unsafe.unsafe(implicit u => FiberRef.unsafe.make(Option.empty[Promise[Nothing, Unit]]))

    /** Runs the app in the real terminal until Ctrl-C or [[quit]]. The terminal is restored when the run ends, also on
      * an interrupt.
      */
    // claude 2026-10-03: created run: build the app in a ZIO Scope, then run the kyo-ui value on the terminal runner
    // inside AmbientZIOs.run (so every ZIO handler runs on the caller's runtime)
    def run(app: ZIO[Scope, Nothing, UI]): UIO[Unit] =
        ZIO.scoped {
            for
                quit <- Promise.make[Nothing, Unit]
                _ <- quitRef.locally(Some(quit)) {
                    for
                        ui <- app
                        _  <- AmbientZIOs.run(KTui.run(withQuit(quit, unsafeToKyo(ui))))
                    yield ()
                }
            yield ()
        }

    /** Ends the run of this app. Call it in a handler: `button("Quit").onClick(Tui.quit)`. Outside a run it does nothing. */
    // claude 2026-10-03: created quit: completes the promise of the active run (found through quitRef)
    val quit: UIO[Unit] =
        quitRef.get.flatMap {
            case Some(p) => p.succeed(()).unit
            case None    => ZIO.unit
        }

    /** The UI, plus one Kyo fiber that waits for the quit promise and then calls the runner's quit. The fiber is started
      * while the runner builds the UI, so it sees the runner's quit action (a Kyo `Local`), and the runner's `Scope`
      * stops it when the run ends.
      */
    // claude 2026-10-03: created withQuit (shared by run and the headless test kit)
    private[ui] def withQuit(quit: Promise[Nothing, Unit], ui: _root_.kyo.UI)(using Frame): _root_.kyo.UI < (Async & KScope) =
        KFiber.init(AmbientZIOs.get(quit.await).andThen(KTui.quit)).andThen(ui)

    // claude 2026-10-03: created setQuit (the test kit sets the quit signal like run does)
    private[ui] def setQuit[R, E, A](quit: Promise[Nothing, Unit])(z: ZIO[R, E, A]): ZIO[R, E, A] =
        quitRef.locally(Some(quit))(z)
end Tui
```

```scala
// source: .work/proto/kyoui-integration/glue/cats/Tui.scala, lines 35-62 (library glue, not app code; integration prototype, DONE)
object Tui:

    /** Runs the app in the real terminal until Ctrl-C. The terminal is restored when the run ends, also on a cancel. */
    // claude 2026-10-03: created run
    def run[F[_]](app: Resource[F, UI])(using F: CEAsync[F]): F[Unit] =
        runWithQuit[F](_ => app)

    /** Runs the app in the real terminal until Ctrl-C or until a handler runs the `quit` action that the app gets. */
    // claude 2026-10-03: created runWithQuit: Dispatcher + quit Deferred + the app's Resource, then the kyo-ui value runs on
    // the terminal runner with the Dispatcher in the facade's ambient Local (AmbientDispatcher)
    def runWithQuit[F[_]](app: F[Unit] => Resource[F, UI])(using F: CEAsync[F]): F[Unit] =
        (for
            d    <- Dispatcher.parallel[F](await = false)
            quit <- Resource.eval(Deferred[F, Unit])
            ui   <- app(quit.complete(()).void)
        yield (d, quit, ui)).use { (d, quit, ui) =>
            CatsBridge.runF(AmbientDispatcher.let(d)(KTui.run(withQuit(d, quit, unsafeToKyo(ui)))))
        }

    /** The UI, plus one Kyo fiber that waits for the quit `Deferred` and then calls the runner's quit. It starts while the
      * runner builds the UI (so it sees the runner's quit action, a Kyo `Local`); the runner's `Scope` stops it.
      */
    // claude 2026-10-03: created withQuit (shared by runWithQuit and the headless test kit)
    private[ui] def withQuit[F[_]](d: Dispatcher[F], quit: Deferred[F, Unit], ui: _root_.kyo.UI)(using
        Frame
    ): _root_.kyo.UI < (Async & KScope) =
        KFiber.init(CatsBridge.getF(quit.get)(using d).andThen(KTui.quit)).andThen(ui)
end Tui
```

Block 1 has 16 non-blank lines (12 without comment-only lines), for four mains.

| Fact | Integration glue |
| --- | --- |
| What the user calls | ZIO: `Tui.run(app: ZIO[Scope, Nothing, UI]): UIO[Unit]` and `Tui.quit: UIO[Unit]` (glue/zio/Tui.scala:45, 60). Cats: `Tui.run[F[_]](app: Resource[F, UI])(using Async[F]): F[Unit]` and `Tui.runWithQuit[F[_]](app: F[Unit] => Resource[F, UI]): F[Unit]` (glue/cats/Tui.scala:39, 45). The mains extend `ZIOAppDefault` or `IOApp.Simple`. Mains.scala has no Kyo import. |
| How a handler runs | ZIO: the whole run is inside `AmbientZIOs.run(KTui.run(...))`, so a ZIO handler runs on the runtime of the caller of `Tui.run` (glue/zio/Tui.scala:52). Cats: a `Dispatcher.parallel[F](await = false)` goes into the facade's `AmbientDispatcher` (glue/cats/Tui.scala:47-51). |
| Quit | ZIO: `Tui.quit` is one global value; it finds the active run through a `FiberRef` (glue/zio/Tui.scala:35-38, 60-64). Cats: the app gets an `F[Unit]` that quits, as the parameter of `runWithQuit`. Both start one Kyo fiber that waits for the signal and then calls the runner's `Tui.quit` (`withQuit`). The facade apps have no quit key; Ctrl-C quits (comment at Mains.scala:8). |
| Run evidence | Logs of the integration agent (read here, not re-run): ZioOnTerminalSuite 6/6 and CatsOnTerminalSuite 6/6 in each of 3 runs (`logs/test-final-c-{1,2,3}.log`), on the runner's headless `TestBackend`; negative controls fail as intended. Real PTY: ZIO Counter 10/10 terminal checks and 22/22 screen checks, `stty -a` after = before (`logs/pty-checklist.log`); the Cats Counter gives the same result. Under pinned CPU contention, 1 of 2 runs failed one Cats test (the runner's first-key race, integration REPORT R2). |
| Known issues (integration REPORT) | A button in a column takes the full width (100 cells). Runner problems found by the integration (not fixed): R1 an interrupted run leaks about 1.75 MB (region watchers), R2 a first-key race, R3 the output guard misses scala.Console.out (a println corrupts the screen). |

## Differences that matter for the decision

Facts only. Each item names its evidence.

1. What the user writes.
   - Current core: one immutable state, `update(state, event): Next[S]`, `view(state): View`, a `Keymap`, and
     `sources(state)` for background work. No component abstraction: the Counter has one number.
   - kyo-ui runner: UI values with signals. State is one or more Kyo refs. Handlers write the refs. A component is a
     function (hooks) or a `Component` subclass. Two independent counters are two calls (`counter("Left")`,
     `counter("Right")`) or two values (`CounterBox("Left")`, `CounterBox("Right")`).
   - Facades: the same kyo-ui model with ZIO or `F[_]` values in the handlers and in the hooks.
2. Effect types in the user's code.
   - Current core Counter (all three ecosystems): no effect type. The Todo and Dashboard of the core use Kyo types
     (`Sync`, `Abort`, `Stream`, `Async`) only for background work.
   - kyo-ui runner: Kyo types in every app, also in the Counter (`UI < Sync`, `SignalRef`, `KyoApp`), and handlers
     typed `Any < Async`.
   - Facades: no Kyo import and no Kyo effect type. Kyo DATA types stay reachable through aliases (facades REPORT
     O2).
3. Where state lives and who owns it.
   - Current core: one value in the engine. Each frame shows one state value.
   - kyo-ui runner: many refs. Hooks: made when the effect runs (top `for`) or at mount (`component(...)`).
     Component class: the runner makes one ref per instance at mount and keeps it by position and class.
   - Facades: refs from `useSignal` that are the same Kyo cell that kyo-ui binds. The facade `Component.mount`
     makes the ref when the app `for` runs; it is not kept by position in a runner.
4. How the screen changes.
   - Current core: the whole view is rebuilt and painted after each change; jatatui writes only the changed cells
     (RenderLoop.scala:181-185 @ feat/core-3-terminal).
   - kyo-ui runner: only the changed regions are repainted. One `+` writes 1 cell, 26 bytes (runner REPORT N4,
     N6). A settle step makes a frame wait for all consequences of an event; it is "very likely" glitch-free, not
     certain (N2). An exact fix needs a change in Kyo (runner REPORT, upstream proposal 1).
   - Latency numbers exist for both, from different machines: old core bench B4 p50 1.56 ms, p99 3.91 ms (macOS);
     runner Counter p50 0.63 ms, p99 1.24 ms (Linux container). The runner REPORT says that this is not a direct
     comparison.
5. Traps.
   - Current core: `Next[S]` is a union, so the result type of `update` must be written (App.scala:95); the Kyo
     `Stream.unfold` chunk size (DashboardApp.scala:30-31); the `fs2.*` import clash (Cats).
   - kyo-ui runner: the lift trap. A handler without the type `Any < Async` compiles and never runs, with no error
     and no warning (Todo.scala:85-94; runner REPORT O5; reproduced by the verifier).
   - Facades: the lift trap fails at compile time with a tui4s message (generated `compiletime.error` overloads).
     Cats only: a foreign `SignallingRef` in a binding setter fails at run time (O3).
6. Widgets and layout.
   - Current core: jatatui widgets (gauge, sparkline, tabs, list, table) through its own `View` DSL.
   - kyo-ui runner: kyo-ui HTML elements with flexbox layout in cells. No built-in gauge or sparkline (the Dashboard
     draws them as text). No scrolling, overlays, mouse or `onKeyUp`; 1 px = 1 cell (runner REPORT N7, N8).
7. Facade parity.
   - Old facades: the Counter text is the same in Kyo, ZIO and Cats except the package and the import (the branch
     also has `examples/src/parity/CounterBody.scala.txt` and `ParitySuite`). The old facades have no Todo.
   - New facades: the ZIO and Cats apps are near copies of each other. They are not the same text as the runner
     apps (other features, ids for the test runner, `update` instead of `updateAndGet`). The new facades have no
     Dashboard.
8. How far each variant was run.
   - Current core: CI green on PR 5 with a Linux terminal job; the macOS expect checklist passed 47/47 (HANDOFF).
     Old ZIO facade: 14 confirmed findings not fixed. Old Cats facade: review not started.
   - kyo-ui runner: headless tests and a real PTY run (Counter and Todo) green on this Linux machine (verifier).
     The Dashboard has no PTY run.
   - Facades: in the facades prototype, a headless test runner only (kyo-ui's own HTML renderer). The integration
     prototype (DONE) runs the unchanged ZIO and Cats Counter and Todo on the terminal runner's headless
     `TestBackend`: 6/6 and 6/6 in each of 3 runs, and a real PTY run of the ZIO and Cats Counter passes.
9. Coverage of the effect points (facades). Drag and drop has no ZIO or Cats form yet: 9 setters are skipped
   (facades REPORT O1). So "ZIO / F[_] types at every effect point" is not yet true.
10. Entry points.
   - Current core: `object X extends TuiApp[S]`. `TuiApp` is a Kyo main, a `ZIOAppDefault` (ZIO) or an
     `IOApp.Simple` (Cats).
   - kyo-ui runner: `object X extends KyoApp: run(Tui.run(app))`.
   - Facades (integration prototype): `object X extends ZIOAppDefault: def run = Tui.run(app)` or
     `object X extends IOApp.Simple: def run: IO[Unit] = Tui.run(app)`. To quit from a handler, ZIO uses the
     global `Tui.quit`; Cats uses the `F[Unit]` that `Tui.runWithQuit` gives to the app.
